checks: The coordinates (t,s) have determinant of absolute value one and send T heights to [−2,1]. The tangent translation of A by a fixed vector and K by half that vector preserves midpoint inclusion, the cut and all areas. It makes the selected full-height segment vertical in these coordinates.

The sets S+B and A+B are nested and have the same height projection. The left and right endpoint gains are nonnegative and sum to the section-width gain. At each t in [−t₊,h], adding the rightmost B point to (0,t) realizes the rightmost S+B endpoint, while adding it to (a₊(t),t) gives a gain at least a₊(t). The left extreme gives the other integral.

Both integration intervals lie inside [l,h] and contain [2,h], since −2≤t_±≤1. They can overlap as height intervals because left and right gains are separate terms in the section difference. If both t_±=1, the two integrals sum to the exact area above −1.

For fixed s the S+B interval is [l+L_B,h+U_B]. It straddles zero by l<−1 and h>2, so its nonnegative length is h+U_B. Thus the captured area is the physical roof integral, and halving A+B costs the factor four.

At d=2, V=9/2, e=(c,−1−c), v₀=(−1,−1). The parameter s on (s,−s) gives the physical measure ds, and η=1−sqrt(1−2b/9) solves b/V=2η−η². Substituting β=H/3 gives H[3−sqrt(9−2b)]. Source cde78a6346699a8a §4 (11)–(13) has the same individual extreme-point intervals and exact common-body reserve.
